newsitem.title: USA: MSRB answers questions about G-38 consultant rule
newsitem.headline: MSRB answers questions about G-38 consultant rule

text.p: MSRB reminded bond firms Monday they must include all fees paid to consultants, including "success fees," bonuses, expenses and monthly retainers, when they report political activity quarterly to the panel.

In a "Questions and Answers" notice it sent to SEC for approval, Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board stated, "If a consultant is to be paid a success fee, dealers must disclose how the success fee will be arrived at (e.g., a certain percentage of profits)."

The "Rule G-38 Q&A" takes effect immediately even though Securities and Exchange Commission probably will publish it in the Federal Register for comment shortly, Christopher Taylor, MSRB executive director, said in a phone interview.
The notice adds if a dealer makes "discretionary bonuses" to a consultant, those payments also must be reported monthly, as well as monthly retainers and expenses.
Enacted in March, rule G-38 requires dealers to disclose information about their consultant arrangements to the 15-member board, which makes them available to issuers and the public.
Taylor said the board wanted to make sure that success fees, in particular, are "clearly spelled out" in G-38 forms because some firms are omitting them.
Success fees are payments consultants get for successfully winning a bond deal.
The board's Q&A is reprinted below:
Q:Is there specific information concerning the role to be performed by a consultant that a dealer must disclose on Form G-37/G-38?

A: The role to be performed by a consultant may be described in general terms on Form G-37/G-38; however dealers must include the state or geographic area in which the consultant is working on behalf of the dealer.
Q:When providing the information required to be disclosed on Form G-37/G-38, how should dealers describe the consultant's compensation arrangement?

A: Dealers must ensure that the compensation arrangement is clearly described and that it correlates with the information being disclosed concerning the total dollar amount paid to the consultant during the reporting period and the dollar amounts paid in connection with particular municipal securities business.
* For example, if a consultant is paid a monthly retained, the amount of the monthly retainer must be disclosed and the total dollar amount paid during the reporting period must be reported.
* If a consultant is reimbursed for expenses, the amount of the reimbursed expenses must be disclosed either separately or within the total dollar amount paid for the quarter.

* If a consultant is to be paid a success fee, dealers must disclose how the success fee will be arrived at (e.g. a certain percentage of profits). The sum total of the dollar amounts paid to the consultant in connection with particular municipal securities business should equal the total dollar amount paid to the consultant during the reporting period.
* In addition, if any discretionary bonus or similar payment is made, this amount must be included within the total amount paid for the quarter in which it is paid.
Q: What information must a dealer disclose on Form G-37/38 for the dollar amounts paid to a consultant connected with particular municipal securities business?

A: If any payment made during the reporting period is related to a consultant's efforts on behalf of the dealer which resulted in particular municipal securities business, whether the municipal securities business was completed during that or a prior reporting period, then the dealer must separtely identify that business and the dollar amount of the payment.

Q: Rule G-38 requires a dealer to disclose in writing its consulting arrangements to an issuer with which it is engaging or seeking to engage in municipal securities business and this written disclosure must include, among other things, the compensation arrangements. What is the level of disclosure required to issuers of the compensation arrangement with consultants?
A: The written disclosure to issuers of the compensation arrangements must explain the arrangement.
* For example, if a consultant is paid a monthly retainer, the amount of the monthly retainer must be disclosed.
* If a consultant also is reimbursed for expenses, this fact must be noted.
* If a consultant is to be paid a success fee, the dealer must disclose to the issuer how that fee will be arrived at (e.g., a certain percentage of profits).
-Vicky Stamas, 202-898-8314
